//: Foundry ADOPTER PROJECT INVENTORY + the meta-repo MANIFEST (the WHAT, workspace-side). Generic foundry/ primitives resolve project-specifics (repo paths, boot command, conventions, live-seam drivers) from HERE rather than hardcoding them. This is ALSO the multi-repo control-plane manifest: to host an infra/service repo as a gitignored sibling subdir, add it under repos{} keyed by a target_repo dispatch key — see docs/control-plane.md (the operating model) and docs/SETUP.md 'Multi-repo control plane' (the add-a-repo runbook). Seeded self-only (path '.'), the single-repo default. Captured + updated by /foundry:init. Sibling of .claude/foundry-operators.json (identity). RULE: never bake a project-specific value into a foundry/ primitive — reference this file by key.

project.name: REPLACE-ME
project.description: REPLACE-ME — one line: what this project is, who it's for. (This workspace is the control plane; the product/infra repos it builds are hosted as gitignored siblings, see repos{} + docs/control-plane.md.)

repos.//: ADD AN ENTRY ONLY ONCE THE REPO IS CLONED. Nothing validates repos{} today — /foundry:doctor's five checks do not read it — and a dangling entry does not fail loudly later: it makes /foundry:authorize skip five grounding floors with a printed 'warn: ... degraded' line and freeze the contract anyway. See docs/control-plane.md section 4.

workspace.role: the control plane itself (the WHAT — specs, governance, the manifest). Self entry: resolves to the workspace root. This alone is the single-repo default — a contract with no target_repo is workspace-targeted.

repos.//hosted-repo-example: To host an infra/service repo, add a sibling entry once you've cloned it into the gitignored subdir, e.g.: "infra": { "path": "infra", "kind": "infra-repo", "role": "the project's IaC (OpenTofu/Kubernetes)" }. The key is the target_repo dispatch key. Runbook: docs/SETUP.md 'Multi-repo control plane'.

surfaces.//: App-exercise binding: surface kind -> how a live-seam human-equivalent walk exercises it (the generic analog of 'make dev + Chrome MCP'). /foundry:init captures this for your app. NOTE: this block is declarative today — no shipped check reads it. The boot recipe /foundry:certify-local actually uses comes from the active stack profile's app_exercise_binding.boot.
